note: Realistic filled-in states in the scoring engine's shape. `expected` is computed by `bin/test-personas --update` and verified by `bin/test-personas`. `hasCriticalFinding` covers only DVT present and aneurysm — a large lesion (>= 30mm) is its own dedicated major-severity trigger (R-SEV-MAJOR-02), entirely separate from the critical-classification predicate, so a large indeterminate mass escalates only to 'urgent' follow-up, not 'critical-alert'. The second persona below isolates exactly that distinction.

personas.name: normal-abdominal-ultrasound-complete
personas.description: A normal abdominal ultrasound for non-specific abdominal discomfort: liver, gallbladder, pancreas, spleen, and kidneys normal in size and echotexture, no mass, cyst, gallstones, hydronephrosis, free fluid, or organomegaly, every mandatory report section present — expect normal classification + none severity + 100% completeness + routine follow-up + no-action.

state.impression: Normal abdominal ultrasound; no structural abnormality identified.
state.recommendedFollowUp: No further ultrasound follow-up required for this indication.

personas.name: abnormal-large-indeterminate-hepatic-mass-major-not-critical-complete
personas.description: A liver ultrasound for deranged liver function tests and right upper quadrant discomfort shows a well-defined, heterogeneous 35mm right hepatic lobe mass with no biliary dilatation, ascites, DVT, or aneurysm: the 30mm large-lesion threshold (R-SEV-MAJOR-02) is a dedicated severity trigger entirely separate from `hasCriticalFinding` (DVT present or aneurysm only), so this grades major severity but escalates only to 'urgent' follow-up, never critical-alert; report complete — expect abnormal classification + major severity (reportingCategory large-lesion) + 100% completeness + urgent follow-up + specialist-referral.

state.clinicalHistory: Deranged liver function tests and right upper quadrant discomfort; liver ultrasound to investigate.
state.comparisonWithPrevious: No previous liver ultrasound on file.
state.findingsNarrative: A well-defined, heterogeneous mass is seen in the right lobe of the liver, measuring 35mm, with mixed echogenicity. No biliary duct dilatation, ascites, or other focal lesion. Gallbladder and pancreas (as visualised) normal.
state.impression: Indeterminate 35mm right hepatic lobe mass, mixed echogenicity; further characterisation with contrast-enhanced CT or MRI recommended.
state.recommendedFollowUp: Refer for contrast-enhanced CT or MRI liver for further characterisation; discuss at the hepatobiliary MDT.

expected.recommendedAction: Arrange urgent clinical review and expedite onward referral.

personas.name: critical-extensive-lower-limb-dvt-uncommunicated-incomplete
personas.description: A left leg venous Doppler for acute calf swelling and pain shows non-compressible, echogenic thrombus within the common femoral and popliteal veins with absent flow, in keeping with an extensive acute left lower-limb DVT: DVT present is a critical structured finding that auto-escalates classification to critical and follow-up to critical-alert regardless of the other axes; the result has not yet been recorded as communicated, no originating request is linked, and the clinical history, comparison, and impression sections are not yet completed while urgent anticoagulation is arranged — expect critical classification + major severity + 40% completeness + critical-alert follow-up + urgent-review.

state.findingsNarrative: Non-compressible, echogenic thrombus is seen within the left common femoral and popliteal veins, with absent flow on Doppler, in keeping with an extensive acute left lower-limb deep vein thrombosis.
state.clinicianNotes: Phoned through to the referring team immediately; urgent anticoagulation being arranged per local DVT pathway.
